summary: Count backward by ones from 20 down to 0.
Count backward from any starting number up to 20.
See a small group of up to 5 objects and name how many without counting (subitizing).
Recognize a penny, know it is worth one cent, and count up to 20 pennies.
Use counting and quick recognition of grouped amounts (ten frames) to explain adding and subtracting within 20.
Add and subtract within 20 with strategies like making ten; the within-10 fluency part is its own standard.
Fluently add and subtract within 10 using mental strategies such as counting on and making ten.
Count forward and backward within 120; read, write, and match numerals to amounts.
Know pennies and dimes and find the value of a mix of them, up to 100 cents.
Use repeated addition to total equal groups or arrays and write a matching equation; no 5-by-5 limit.
Count forward and backward within 1,000; skip-count forward and backward by 5s, 10s, and 100s.
Know how minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, and years relate, such as 7 days in a week.
Recognize nickels, quarters, and dollar bills and know what each is worth.
Gather data with interviews, surveys, and observations to answer questions about interests or surroundings.
Given a rule for a number sequence, spot and explain features the rule does not state; shape patterns dropped.
Fluently add and subtract whole numbers up to 1,000,000 with any efficient algorithm, not only the standard one.
Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers with an algorithm such as partial products or the standard one.
Divide up to four-digit by two-digit whole numbers, now including the standard long-division algorithm.

state_code: # - Iowa Academic Standards for Mathematics (adopted by the State Board April 29, 2024; document dated April 2024):
# - Implementation Resources Guidebook (links the official crosswalk and spreadsheet): https://educate.iowa.gov/media/11752/download?inline
# - Iowa Academic Standards for Mathematics Crosswalk, 2010 vs 2024 (8/4/2025, Google Drive file linked from guidebook):
# - Iowa's 2010 math standards were the CCSS, so the crosswalk is effectively a CCSS crosswalk.
# - CCSS-style Grade.Domain.ClusterLetter.Number (K.CC.A.1, 2.MD.C.8); all 148 CCSS K-5 codes are kept with the same numbers.
# - Iowa-only additions insert "IA": Grade.Domain.IA.ClusterLetter.Number (K.CC.IA.A.1, 1.OA.IA.C.2, 2.MD.IA.D.1). 10 such standards in K-2.
# - Sub-points are bulleted, not lettered as separate codes; folded into each standard.
# DOMAINS (K-5): CC Counting and Cardinality (K); OA Operations and Algebraic Thinking; NBT Number and Operations in Base Ten;
#   NF Number and Operations - Fractions (3-5); MD Measurement and Data; G Geometry.
#   Clusters are labelled Major / Supporting / Additional.
# - None. 1.OA.C.6's within-10 fluency part was split into 1.OA.IA.C.2.
# - Counting backward (K.CC.IA.A.1-A.2; backward counting added to 1.NBT.A.1, 2.NBT.A.2); subitizing (K.CC.IA.B.1, 1.OA.IA.C.1).
# - Money from kindergarten: penny (K), pennies and dimes (1), nickels/quarters/dollars (2.MD.IA.C.2).
# - Units-of-time relationships incl. days/weeks/months/years (2.MD.IA.C.1); data collection by surveys/interviews (2.MD.IA.D.1).
# - Fluency notes name strategies; 4.NBT.B.4/5.NBT.B.5 accept any efficient algorithm; 5.NBT.B.6 adds the standard division algorithm.
# - Many standards add Iowa notes/examples and "See Problem Types Table" references; treated as same.
# - Iowa's crosswalk gives no change labels, only side-by-side text; kinds here come from comparing the 2024 text with CCSS text.
# - Coin standards in K and 1 marked "moved" from 2.MD.C.8; 2.MD.IA.C.2 marked "edited" on 2.MD.C.8 (same grade).
# - 2.MD.IA.C.1 marked "new"; its minutes/hours part overlaps CCSS 4.MD.A.1.
# - 1.OA.IA.C.1 mapped to 1.OA.C.5 (its part a restates 1.OA.C.5); the subitizing part has no CCSS code.
# - 4.OA.C.5 marked edited because generating shape patterns is gone; 2.OA.C.4 because the 5x5 array limit is gone.
# - The page states the adoption date only; no separate implementation deadline was found. Treated as current for 2026-27.
